text: Plan an exploration-led economy. Scout nearby candidates before committing the Ark; develop a science world and a production center rather than repeat the prior compact beacon rush.

The west is extensively charted, but its best worlds are behind or beside Veyr. Avoid a distant unsupported colony; the Ark will settle Nacre within the home network. The held home frigate has no actionable threat and should not force an extra warning.

Solace reached8/8. Build Habitation before factory/Forge development so another population step can open a fifth slot; comparison explicitly preserves the current12 production during this construction. Delay the fifth Ark a few cycles rather than replace the capital science investment.

Meridian creates a real shared border: the public relation now shows8 Choir grievance and trust24. Keep the treaty, but move the existing frigate toward that frontier. Save minerals this cycle rather than commission another low-priority building; several labs and the capital Habitat have just finished.

Sundrift has reached six population and supports an Extraction Charter. Commit120 credits and60 minerals for+6 minerals per cycle; retain its market/lab/mine rather than replace science to manufacture more ore. Factory at the capital follows once the treasury recovers.

Stillwater90%/rich5/science4 contains an intact Observatory. Immediate65 minerals would ease the current bottleneck, but this is a plausible long-lived research colony. Leave the choice intact until20 minerals can fund preservation, then send the next Ark here rather than nearby Haven. This takes a remote settlement/lab and time; no restoration benefit is assumed yet.

Plotted the Ark’s8-jump course from Sundrift to Stillwater. It crosses Veyr-held Sable under our active trade agreement; seven stops have unknown current opposition. The route is a plan, not a safety guarantee. Meridian’s single frigate remains on Hold.

Forge I at Solace changes22→29 production and Vanguard2→1 cycle, a useful threshold. Fund it before building a navy. Research now follows the Asterion Protocol while the fourth lab and a future remote colony increase science; no rival beacon is yet public.

Cycle27 public sovereignty changes Stillwater to Khar. Our preserved Observatory is now theirs; the long colony voyage lost the race. Do not force war for sunk preservation costs. Kepler, where the Ark already is, offers76% habitability, native3 science and proximity to Nacre. Settle there instead and let the new research colony support the Protocol.

Three home frigates are assembled, with one further commission to make four. After that, pause naval spending and reserve minerals for Beacon construction and colony production. The fifth colony/laboratory and Academy finish soon; quiet diplomacy gives time to build the network, but public rival beacons will change that priority.

Nacre’s Academy has finished. Add a factory there now: the comparison shows9→15 production, important for a future140-work Beacon. The capital yard is deliberately idle with four frigates staged at Nacre and one at Meridian; minerals are being saved for the network.

Sundrift reached nine population, opening its fifth slot. Add its factory before the Protocol finishes; Nacre and Sundrift need the slow Beacon work started first, while Solace’s29-production Forge can finish the third node later. Existing five-frigate readiness is enough to preserve the mineral reserve for now.

Stillwater’s live expedition record now shows the actual continuation: Khar published the last atlas in cycle35, receiving140 science and30 credits. Our preservation history at20 remains. The material opportunity cost is real; no inference is made about Khar research timing beyond this recorded reward.

The unfunded Sundrift Beacon comparison remains inspectable. Plan to replace its Exchange Port, losing7 credits each cycle while preserving the Extraction-support mine, lab, factory and growing population. Net income is already105 and treasury1320, so the60-credit alignment payment remains sustainable.

The new cruiser quote is65 credits/77 minerals and three cycles at Solace. It is not affordable this cycle. One cruiser before the capital Beacon will add a heavier formation for the exposed network, at the cost of roughly one cycle to the final node; no rival completed Beacons are public yet.

Deflector Fields completes44. Research Stellar Accords next so Distributed Command can eventually give the staged warships a second jump; better defensive response matters once the first two Beacons become public. Current borders remain peaceful, so there is no justification for a pre-emptive war.

Correction to the cycle44 decision note: Deflector Fields had212/220, not completion. I switched too early; the UI transferred accumulated science and completed Stellar Accords instead. This was my research-reading mistake, not a driver failure or rollback. The actual archives now show Shields still available for220 and128 stored science. Select it again;96 per cycle should finish it next cycle. Distributed Command actually costs500, so its mobility improvement will come later.

The final Beacon replaces Solace’s Habitat. The actual comparison explicitly preserves12 citizens while capacity becomes8 and natural growth stays paused; production, income and Forge support remain unchanged. This preserves the mineral mine and shipyard for defense. Commission at46 after the cruiser completes; expected construction is five cycles under current conditions.

Nacre now has a mixed defensive group: four frigates136 hull and one cruiser85 hull. Assign the four-frigate formation as defensive lead for1 order, keeping the larger total hull/firepower first. The UI correctly warns that formations fight separately and this does not guarantee the cruiser protection. Add a Bastion on the exposed Meridian frontier while all three Beacons are already funded.

No hostile military is in local sensors yet; an enemy civilian Ark is at Kepler. Defend our network rather than chase their distant beacons. We have cash and ore for continued one-cycle frigates.
